  text: 'Then those whose rods were green but cracked handed them in. All handed in green rods and stood
    in their own group. The shepherd rejoiced over them because they had all changed and put away their
    cracks.


    2. Those whose rods were half green and half dry also handed them in. Some rods were found completely
    green, some half dry, some dry and eaten away, and some green with shoots. All these people were dismissed,
    each to their own group.


    3. Then those whose rods were two-thirds green and one-third dry handed them in. Many handed in green
    rods, many half-dry ones, and others dry ones that were eaten away. All stood in their own group.


    4. Then those whose rods were two-thirds dry and one-third green handed them in. Many handed in half-dry
    rods; some handed in dry ones that were eaten away, some half-dry ones with cracks, and a few green
    ones. All stood in their own group.[a]


    5. Those whose rods had been green, with a very small dry part and cracks, handed them in. Some handed
    in green rods, and some green rods with shoots. They too went to their own group.[b]


    6. Then those whose rods had only a little green, with the remaining parts dry, handed them in. Their
    rods were found mostly green, with shoots and fruit on the shoots, while others were entirely green.
    The shepherd rejoiced very greatly over these rods because they were found in this condition. Each
    person went to their own group.[c]'
